content:
Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE: BE ) jumped after trading on September 4 after it was announced that the stock had been added to the S&P 500, marking an important milestone for the company. The change will be effective prior to the open of trading on September 21, to coincide with the quarterly rebalance.

Bloom Energy has now surged by over 150% since the beginning of 2026, propelled by its growing role as a potential power provider for the booming AI data center industry. The fuel-cell power company had the strongest quarter in its history in Q2, easily exceeding expectations and delivering a revenue growth of over 166% compared to last year.

The strong demand for its power solutions also prompted Bloom to raise its full-year revenue outlook to the range of $3.9 billion to $4.2 billion, representing 100% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

S&P 500 Inclusion Adds Fuel to Bloom's Rally: 

The inclusion in the illustrious S&P 500 could increase Bloom Energy's exposure to institutional investors and generate additional demand from funds that track the benchmark. More importantly, the addition comes at a time when the company is gaining traction in the AI power market.

Bloom currently has an agreement with Oracle to supply the hyperscaler with up to 2.8 ​GW of fuel cell capacity, highlighting the value of its technology as data center operators seek power solutions that are quicker to deploy than conventional grid connections. Additionally, Bloom Energy also expanded its partnership with Brookfield Asset Management this summer, boosting their funding framework fivefold to $25 billion to accelerate the global deployment of the company's ​fuel cells.

Successfully converting these partnerships into large-scale deployments, and the addition of new ones, should continue to accelerate the growth of Bloom's revenue and cash flows.

While the inclusion in the S&P 500 could provide a temporary catalyst, Bloom Energy's long-term performance will ultimately depend on its underlying fundamentals. A high-growth narrative without a corresponding uptick in financial performance could expose the stock to a significant valuation correction.

The concerns of a potential AI bubble also present a significant risk. Hyperscalers are currently committing hundreds of billions of dollars to expand their data center capacity, but the long-term returns on these investments are still uncertain. Any meaningful slowdown in AI adoption, weaker-than-expected returns, or a subsequent pullback in capital spending could significantly weaken the projected power demand from data centers.

Bloom Energy's inclusion in the S&P 500 marks a major milestone for the company and could help expand the institutional demand for its stock. However, its long-term investment case still depends on sustained revenue growth, successful execution of AI data center partnerships, and its ability to convert strong demand into sustainable earnings and cash flow growth.

Bloom Energy Corporation (NYSE:BE) was held by 116 hedge funds in the Insider Monkey database at the end of Q2 2026, with a total investment value of around $10.8 billion. This is up from 91 hedge fund investors with a total stake value of just under $4.5 billion in the previous quarter.

While we acknowledge the potential of BE as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk.
